text: Where to get it Every version is published on the Releases page, with a .sha256 file next to each download so you can check it. The site, openwhisper.entringer.dev, links to the same files. The first release is for Windows. The Mac version ships once Apple has signed and notarized it. It will install with Homebrew or a .dmg, as described below.   Platform   Download   Checksum file    --- --- ---    Windows   Open.Whisper_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe   Open.Whisper_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe.sha256     Mac   Not yet: it ships once Apple has signed it   —   X.Y.Z is the version number. Get Open Whisper only from that page or, once the Mac version ships, from Homebrew: those are the official channels.

What your computer needs     Windows   Mac    --- --- ---    System   Windows 10 (22H2) or Windows 11, 64-bit   macOS 14 Sonoma or later     Processor   Intel or AMD with AVX2 (Intel from 2013, AMD from 2015)   Apple Silicon or Intel, one download for both     Disk space   Under 300 MB   About 200 MB     Internet   Only during installation, if WebView2 is missing   Not needed once downloaded     Account   None   None   On a Windows PC with an ARM processor, Open Whisper runs under emulation, not natively. On Windows, transcription runs on the processor; it does not use the graphics card.

Install on Windows On the Releases page, download Open.Whisper_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe and the .sha256 file next to it. Check the download (below): it tells you the file is the one that was published. Open the installer. If Windows shows Windows protected your PC, choose More info, then Run anyway. Follow the installer. It installs for your user only and never asks for an administrator password. It picks English or Portuguese on its own, and shows the terms of use. Start Open Whisper from the Start menu if it is not running yet. Its icon appears in the notification area, next to the clock, and the setup window opens: see First run. Check the download Open Command Prompt or PowerShell in the folder where you saved the installer, and run: Open the .sha256 file in Notepad. The long string of letters and digits that certutil prints must be the same as the one in that file. If it is not, delete the installer and download it again from the Releases page. The first Windows release is not signed with a code-signing certificate yet, and SmartScreen warns before it runs an installer that is not signed. Checking the hash is how you confirm the file is the one published. WebView2 Open Whisper's windows are drawn by Microsoft Edge WebView2. If it is missing from your PC, the installer downloads and installs it by itself, without asking. That is the only moment the installation needs the internet. The open-whisper command The installer also puts the open-whisper command on your user PATH, for the command line. Open a new Command Prompt or PowerShell window after installing: windows that were already open do not see it. If your user PATH was already very long, the installer leaves it untouched so it cannot damage it. Run the command by its full path instead: open-whisper.com, in the folder where Open Whisper was installed.

Install on the Mac With Homebrew This installs Open Whisper in Applications and puts the open-whisper command on your PATH. With the .dmg On the Releases page, download Open.Whisper_X.Y.Z_universal.dmg and the .sha256 file next to it, into the same folder. Check the download. In Terminal, in that folder, run: shasum -a 256 -c Open.Whisper_X.Y.Z_universal.dmg.sha256 It must answer OK. If it does not, delete the .dmg and download it again. Open the .dmg and drag Open Whisper into the Applications folder. Open Open Whisper from Applications. Its icon appears in the menu bar and the setup window opens: see First run. Keep the app directly in Applications (or in the Applications folder inside your home folder). Opened from the .dmg, from Downloads or from a subfolder, it cannot turn on Open at login. Installed from the .dmg, the open-whisper command is not on your PATH yet: Command line shows the one-line link that puts it there. Signed and notarized The Mac version is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so macOS can confirm who made it and that it was not changed. It is not in the Mac App Store: pasting into other apps needs the Accessibility permission, and the App Store's sandbox does not allow it.

Update to a new version Open Whisper does not check for updates and never goes online to look for them. New versions appear on the Releases page; you can follow them with its feed, https://github.com/fabricio-entringer/open-whisper-public/releases.atom. With Homebrew: run brew upgrade --cask open-whisper. With the .dmg: quit Open Whisper from its menu, download and check the new .dmg, and drag the app into Applications again, replacing the old one. Quit Open Whisper from its menu. Download and check the new installer. Run it the same way. Your settings and downloaded models are kept.
Uninstall How to remove Open Whisper, and which files it leaves behind, is in Data and uninstalling.
What your computer needs, and how to download, check and install Open Whisper on Windows and, once it ships, on the Mac.

The welcome screen The window opens on 100% on your Mac (on Windows, 100% on your PC), with one line per step: Microphone: to hear you, only while you dictate. Paste: so the text lands where your cursor is. Shortcut: the only setting, and it comes ready. Test: your first dictation, for real. Microphone: to hear you, only while you dictate. Shortcut: the only setting, and it comes ready. Test: your first dictation, for real. There is no Paste step: Windows needs no permission for Open Whisper to paste. The screen also says where the icon is: in the notification area, next to the clock, or behind ^ (see Where the icon lives). Press Get started. The steps are named along the top of the window: you can pick any of them at any time, with the mouse or the arrow keys.

Microphone This is the one permission dictation cannot work without. The window says when the microphone is on (only while you dictate, never in the background), where transcription happens (on this computer, with no internet) and what is kept afterwards (nothing: the audio is discarded, never saved to disk). Press Allow microphone. macOS asks whether Open Whisper may use the microphone. Click Allow. The window says Microphone ready. and moves to the next step. The window says Microphone access is off. Open Settings and switch Open Whisper on — dictation needs it. Press Open Settings: System Settings opens at Privacy & Security → Microphone. Switch Open Whisper on and come back to the window, which notices the change. Windows does not ask: its privacy settings decide whether apps may use the microphone. Press Check the microphone. If nothing blocks it, the window says Microphone ready. and moves to the next step. The window says Windows is blocking the microphone. Open Settings, turn on “Let desktop apps access your microphone”, and come back here. Press Open Windows Settings: Settings opens at Privacy & security → Microphone. Turn on Let desktop apps access your microphone and come back to the window, which notices the change.

Paste (Mac only) With the Accessibility permission, Open Whisper pastes the text for you. The window says what it does (sends ⌘V to the app you are in), what it does not (it never reads your screen or what you type) and what happens without it (the text goes to the clipboard and you paste it with ⌘V). Press Enable auto-paste. macOS offers to open System Settings. There, under Accessibility, switch Open Whisper on. Come back to the window. When it sees the permission, it says Auto-paste ready. and moves on. macOS often applies this permission only when the app opens again. The window then says so and shows Reopen Open Whisper. Press it: the app closes, opens again a second later, and setup picks up where it was. You can also press Skip — I'll paste manually. Setup goes on, and every dictation waits on the clipboard for you to paste with ⌘V. You can turn auto-paste on later: see Where the text lands. On Windows this step does not exist.

Shortcut The shortcut comes ready: ⇧⌘Space on the Mac, Ctrl+Shift+Space on Windows. It is the only setup Open Whisper needs. Keep the shortcut shown, or click its key and press the new combination. Esc keeps the current one. Pick the mode. Hold to Talk records while you hold the keys and transcribes when you let go. Toggle: press once to start and again to stop. Press Continue. Both choices are saved the moment you make them. A shortcut needs a modifier key; the rules, and the combinations the system keeps for itself, are in Settings. The modes are explained in Dictate.

Test The last step is a real dictation, pasted into the window's test field the same way it is pasted into any app. In Hold to Talk, hold the shortcut, say a sentence and let go. In Toggle, press the shortcut, say a sentence and press it again. Watch the text arrive in the field. The status line under it says what happened:   The window says   What happened    --- ---    On air. Go ahead.   It is recording.     Transcribing…   You stopped; the text is on its way.     It's here. In any app, the text goes wherever your cursor is.   The text landed in the field.     The text was pasted where the cursor was, outside this field. Click the field and try again.   The cursor was somewhere else when the text arrived.     No speech was heard. Try again, closer to the microphone.   The recording had no speech in it, so nothing was pasted.     Cancelled with Esc. Nothing was transcribed.   You pressed Esc while it was recording.     Without microphone access the test can't record. Turn it on in the Microphone step.   The microphone permission is missing.   When the text could not be pasted, it waits on the clipboard and the window says so: The text is on the clipboard. Paste it here with ⌘V. Auto-paste is off, so the text went to the clipboard. Paste it here with ⌘V. You skipped the Paste step or did not give the permission. The text is on the clipboard. Paste it here with Ctrl+V. The note at the bottom of the window says whether Esc cancels with the shortcut and mode you chose. With Hold to Talk and Ctrl+Shift+Space it says While you hold this shortcut, Esc doesn't cancel: with these keys it belongs to Windows. In Toggle mode, Esc cancels. There, let go of the keys to finish. See Cancel with Esc. Any other problem shows the same message as its notification: see Dictate. Open at login This step also shows the Open at login switch, off unless it was already on in the system. Turn it on if you want Open Whisper to start when you log in to your computer. Finishing setup never changes it. On the Mac it works only with the app directly in Applications. When you are done, press Done. The window closes and setup is complete.

section: If you close it before Done
text: If you close it before Done Esc, ⌘. or ⌘W close the window (Ctrl+W on Windows). What you already chose stays saved: the permissions, the shortcut and the mode. Setup is not marked complete, though, so the window opens again the next time Open Whisper starts. On the Mac, after the app reopens, it goes to the first step still missing. Everything the setup sets can also be changed later: the shortcut, the mode and Open at login in Settings, the permissions in the system's settings.

Where the icon lives Open Whisper has no main window. After setup, it lives in an icon, and its menu is how you reach everything else: see The icon and its menu. The icon is in the menu bar, at the top right, near the clock. There is no icon in the Dock. The icon is in the notification area, next to the clock. Windows 11 often hides new icons behind ^: if you do not see it, click ^ and drag the Open Whisper icon onto the taskbar, so you can see when it is recording.
The setup window that opens the first time: microphone, paste, shortcut and a real test dictation, step by step.

The loop Put the cursor where you want the text, in any app. Hold ⇧⌘Space on the Mac or Ctrl+Shift+Space on Windows, and speak. Let go. The indicator says Transcribing, and the text is pasted where the cursor is. The shortcut works whichever app is in front, and needs no permission. The audio stays on your computer and is discarded once transcribed: see Privacy. If the text does not appear at the cursor, it is waiting on the clipboard: see Where the text lands. Pressing the shortcut while it says Transcribing does nothing: wait for the text, then dictate again. The menu's Start Recording item does the same as the shortcut: see The icon and its menu.

Your shortcut The default is ⇧⌘Space on the Mac and Ctrl+Shift+Space on Windows. You can record another one in Settings. It must include ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ on the Mac, or Ctrl or Alt on Windows. Shift alone does not count, and the Windows key cannot be part of it. Some combinations belong to the system. If you pick one, Settings shows it followed by is reserved by macOS. (on Windows, is reserved by Windows.), and Open Whisper uses ⇧⌘D on the Mac or Ctrl+Shift+D on Windows instead. The menu's Start Recording item always shows the shortcut in use. If another app already holds the combination, Settings shows it followed by could not be registered. Pick another one; until then, Start Recording in the menu still works. Ctrl+Shift+Space also means something in Word (a non-breaking space) and in VS Code. If you use them, choose another shortcut. The full list of keys is in Shortcuts and keys.

Hold to Talk or Toggle   Mode   To start   To stop    --- --- ---    Hold to Talk (default)   Hold the shortcut   Let go     Toggle   Press the shortcut once   Press it again   Change it in Settings, under Mode. It applies at once. Only Toggle can stop by itself after a silence (see When a recording ends by itself).

Cancel with Esc Changed your mind while recording? Press Esc. The audio is thrown away without being transcribed: nothing is pasted, the clipboard is not touched, and the last transcription stays what it was. The indicator shows Cancelled for about a second, with its own sound, and the menu says Open Whisper — Recording cancelled. Open Whisper takes Esc only while it is recording. The rest of the time, Esc reaches your apps as usual. Once the indicator says Transcribing, Esc no longer cancels. In Toggle, press Esc. In Hold to Talk, press Esc while you still hold the shortcut: with the default, that is ⇧⌘Esc. A shortcut that holds both ⌥ and ⌘ cannot cancel in Hold to Talk: ⌥⌘Esc is macOS's Force Quit, so Open Whisper leaves it alone. In Toggle, press Esc. In Hold to Talk with the default Ctrl+Shift+Space, Esc cannot cancel: Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager, so Open Whisper leaves it to Windows. The same goes for shortcuts held with Ctrl alone or Alt alone (Ctrl+Esc opens Start, Alt+Esc switches windows). Letting go of the keys ends the recording and transcribes it. Switch to Toggle, or choose a shortcut held with Ctrl and Alt, such as Ctrl+Alt+Space. Then Ctrl+Alt+Esc cancels while you hold it.

section: When a recording ends by itself
text: When a recording ends by itself Stop after silence (Toggle only) In Toggle, Open Whisper can end the recording once you stop talking. It is off by default. Turn it on in Settings → Advanced → Stop after silence, and pick from 1 to 10 seconds, in half-second steps. The row only appears in Toggle mode. The wait starts only after you have spoken: silence before the first word never ends a recording. Pauses shorter than the time you picked do not end it. Steady room noise counts as silence. A breath or a creak does not keep the recording open. The silence at the end is cut off before transcription. If you press the shortcut within 1.5 seconds after it stopped by itself, Open Whisper takes it as your late "stop" and does not start a new recording. A last phrase spoken so quietly that no voice is heard in it may be left out. Maximum length Every recording, in either mode, stops at a time limit: 120 seconds by default, adjustable from 15 to 1800 seconds (30 minutes) in Settings → Advanced → Max recording. At the limit, what was recorded is transcribed and pasted as usual, and a notification says Recording stopped at the time limit — transcribing what was captured.

Language By default, the language is Auto-detect: it is recognised anew in each dictation, so you can change language from one dictation to the next. If it guesses wrong, pin your language in Settings → Language: there are 16 to choose from, and the change applies at once.

The indicator and the sounds While you dictate, a small indicator appears at the bottom centre of the screen you are using. It stays above every window, full-screen apps included, never takes the focus, and lets clicks pass through.   The indicator says   When    --- ---    Recording   While it records. A red light, and a level meter that follows your voice.     Transcribing   From the moment you stop until the text is delivered.     Error   Briefly, when something failed. A notification says what (see below).     Cancelled   For about a second, after Esc.   It disappears when the dictation is over. A recording starts with the Tink sound and ends with Pop, whether text was delivered, no speech was heard or something failed. A cancel sounds Purr. Open Whisper plays its own sounds: one when recording starts, one when it ends (text delivered, no speech heard or a failure), and one for a cancel. Screen readers (VoiceOver on the Mac, Narrator on Windows) announce when recording starts, when it is cancelled and when there is an error.

When nothing is pasted If the recording had no speech, nothing is pasted and no notification appears: you only hear the end sound. A result with no letters or digits, such as a lone full stop, counts as no speech. Try again, closer to the microphone. Other cases come with a notification:   Notification   What it means    --- ---    Nothing was recorded — check the microphone permission, or hold the shortcut a moment longer.   The press was too short to record anything, or the microphone permission is missing.     Microphone unavailable — check the permission or whether another app is using it.   No microphone is connected, or another app is holding it.     Windows is blocking the microphone. Allow it in Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone, including for desktop apps.   Windows only: the system's privacy settings block the microphone, and nothing was recorded. See Permissions.     Couldn't transcribe that audio. Try again.   The transcription failed. Dictate again.     Couldn't load the speech model. Check Settings.   The chosen model is missing or damaged. In Settings → Advanced → Model, choose Default: see Models.   Check that the system lets Open Whisper use the microphone. System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone: Open Whisper must be on. Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone: Let desktop apps access your microphone must be on. More in Troubleshooting.
Hold the shortcut, speak, let go. The two modes, cancelling with Esc, recordings that end by themselves, language, and what you see and hear.

Pasted at the cursor When the transcription is ready, Open Whisper puts the text on the clipboard and sends the paste shortcut to the app in front, as if you had pressed it. So it works wherever an ordinary paste works. The paste is ⌘V. Sending it to other apps needs the Accessibility permission, which setup asks for (see First run). Before pasting, Open Whisper also asks macOS what kind of element has the focus, a text field or not, so it does not paste into nothing. It looks at the kind of element, not at what is in it, and it never reads your screen or what you type. The paste is Ctrl+V. Windows needs no permission for it. Before pasting, Open Whisper asks Windows what kind of element has the focus, a text field or not, so it does not paste into nothing. It looks at the kind of element, not at what is in it. Stay in the field until the text lands.

Your clipboard is put back After a paste that worked, Open Whisper waits half a second and puts back what you had copied before, as long as the clipboard still holds the transcription. If you copied something else in that half second, it is left alone. Only text is put back. If you had copied an image or formatted content, do not count on getting it back. When the text stays on the clipboard instead (next section), it replaces what you had copied.

section: When the text goes to the clipboard instead
text: When the text goes to the clipboard instead Open Whisper does not paste when it can tell the paste would fail or land nowhere. It leaves the text on the clipboard and shows a notification: Copied to clipboard — paste with ⌘V. This happens when: the Accessibility permission is off; a password field has the focus (macOS's Secure Input is on); nothing that takes text has the focus: the Desktop, a Finder window, a web page you are only reading; the paste could not be sent, or did not go through within 2 seconds. Copied to clipboard — paste with Ctrl+V. This happens when: the window in front runs as administrator, or Open Whisper cannot tell whether it does: Windows does not let an app send keys to a window with higher rights; a password field has the focus; the element with the focus does not take text; the paste could not be sent, or did not go through within 2 seconds. The notification is the same whatever the reason. Click where you want the text and paste it, or use Retry Last Transcription (below). If notifications from Open Whisper are turned off in the system, you will not see this one. The text is on the clipboard all the same.

section: Turn on auto-paste on the Mac
text: Turn on auto-paste on the Mac If you skipped the Paste step during setup, every dictation waits on the clipboard. Settings says so under the shortcut: Automatic paste: off — the shortcut works, and the text goes to the clipboard for you to paste with ⌘V. Press Turn on… in Settings, or choose Enable auto-paste… in the menu. In System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, switch Open Whisper on. If the text still goes to the clipboard, quit Open Whisper and open it again: macOS may apply the permission only to the app opened afterwards. When it is on, Settings says Automatic paste: on — the text is pasted where the cursor is. On Windows there is nothing to turn on: auto-paste needs no permission. See Troubleshooting.

section: Apps that do not say what has the focus
text: Apps that do not say what has the focus Some apps do not tell Open Whisper what has the focus. On the Mac, those are Chrome, VS Code, Slack, Discord and other apps built on Chromium. Open Whisper pastes into them anyway, or it would stop working there. If no text field had the focus in such an app, the paste lands nowhere and your old clipboard is put back: the text is neither at the cursor nor on the clipboard. Get it with Copy Last Transcription (below).

section: Copy or retry the last dictation
text: Copy or retry the last dictation Two items in the menu bring the last dictation back:   Item   What it does    --- ---    Copy Last Transcription   Puts the last dictation's text on the clipboard. Available once a dictation has produced text since Open Whisper started.     Retry Last Transcription   Delivers the same text again: pasted at the cursor, or left on the clipboard by the same rules. It does not transcribe again. Available when there is a last text and Open Whisper is not recording or transcribing.   Open Whisper keeps only the last dictation, only in memory. Quitting forgets it, and there is no history. More about the menu in The icon and its menu.

Windows: clipboard history and sync Whenever Open Whisper puts dictated text on the clipboard, it marks it to stay out of clipboard history (Win+V), out of clipboard sync across your devices, and out of apps that monitor the clipboard. That includes the times the text waits on the clipboard for you: paste it with Ctrl+V, it will not be in Win+V. This keeps what you dictate on this PC. See Privacy.
How the text reaches the cursor, when it waits on the clipboard instead, and how to get your last dictation back.

Where the icon is In the menu bar, at the top right, near the clock. Open Whisper has no icon in the Dock. In the notification area, next to the clock. If you do not see it, click ^ and drag the Open Whisper icon onto the taskbar. Click the icon to open its menu. Only one copy of Open Whisper runs at a time. Opening it again while it is running leaves the running copy in charge: no second icon appears.

What the icon tells you   State   The icon    --- ---    Ready   The plain icon. On the Mac it takes the colour of the other menu-bar icons; on Windows it is white on a dark taskbar and black on a light one.     Recording   Red.     Transcribing and pasting   Pulses. It stays still if motion is reduced in the system (Mac: Accessibility → Reduce motion; Windows: Animation effects off).     Error   Amber, for a moment, then back to ready. A notification says what happened.   A video transcription running in the background does not change the icon: the menu shows its progress instead. Screen readers read the menu's first line, such as Open Whisper — Ready, as the icon's name.

The menu, item by item From top to bottom, with lines separating the groups:   Item   What it does    --- ---    Open Whisper — Ready   The status line. It cannot be clicked. It also reads Recording…, Transcribing…, Delivering… (pasting the text), Error or Recording cancelled.     Start Recording   Starts a dictation, as the shortcut does, and becomes Stop Recording while it records. It works like Toggle in both modes. Shows your shortcut beside it, and is available only when Open Whisper is ready or recording.     Copy Last Transcription   Puts the last dictation's text on the clipboard. See Where the text lands.     Retry Last Transcription   Pastes the last dictation's text again, without transcribing it again. See Where the text lands.     Enable auto-paste…   Mac only: opens System Settings at Accessibility, to turn auto-paste on.     Transcribe YouTube Video…   Opens the video window, for a YouTube link or a video or audio file on your computer. While a video is being transcribed, it shows the progress, such as (42%). See Video and files.     Settings…   Opens Settings.     About Open Whisper   Opens the About window, with the version number. See About, versions and terms.     Quit Open Whisper   Quits the app (see Quitting).   Once Accessibility is on, Enable auto-paste… turns into Auto-paste is on, which cannot be clicked. If you switched it on and it still says Enable auto-paste…, quit Open Whisper and open it again. Windows needs no permission for auto-paste, so the menu has no such item.

section: The keys shown in the menu
text: The keys shown in the menu The menu shows keys beside some items: your dictation shortcut beside Start Recording, ⇧⌘C beside Copy Last Transcription, ⌘, beside Settings… and ⌘Q beside Quit Open Whisper. On Windows they are Ctrl+Shift+C, Ctrl+, and Ctrl+Q. They are not shortcuts that work from any app. Outside the menu, only your dictation shortcut reaches Open Whisper, plus Esc while it is recording. All the keys are listed in Shortcuts and keys.

Quitting Choose Quit Open Whisper. The shortcut stops working until you open the app again, and the last dictation, kept only in memory, is forgotten. If a video is being transcribed, Open Whisper asks first: A video transcription is still running. Quitting now will lose it. Choose Keep running to go on, or Quit anyway to quit and lose that transcription. To have Open Whisper start by itself when you log in, turn on Open at login in Settings.
Where the icon is, what its colours mean, and what each item in its menu does.

Opening and saving Open the Open Whisper menu: click its icon in the menu bar (Mac) or in the notification area (Windows). Choose Settings…. The window is called Settings. Close it with Esc, ⌘. or ⌘W. The window is called Settings. Close it with Esc or Ctrl+W. If Windows is blocking the microphone, the top of Recording says Windows is blocking the microphone, so dictation only hears silence. Allow it in Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone, including for desktop apps. The key Open Windows Settings takes you to the page where you allow it. There is no Save button. Every change applies the moment you make it, and the next dictation uses it. The window fits its content and never scrolls. Everything in it works from the keyboard: Tab moves between fields. When the window comes back to the front, it reads the paste permission and the login item again, so a change you made in the system settings shows up here. The window says Could not save preferences: followed by the reason. Nothing changed. Read the reason, correct the field and try again. A shortcut with no modifier is the usual cause (see the next section).

Recording Shortcut The key in this row shows the shortcut that starts a dictation. The default is ⇧⌘Space on the Mac and Ctrl+Shift+Space on Windows. It works whatever app is in front, and it needs no permission. To change it, see The shortcut recorder below. Under the shortcut, one line says whether the text is pasted for you: Automatic paste: on — the text is pasted where the cursor is. Automatic paste: off — the shortcut works, and the text goes to the clipboard for you to paste with ⌘V. Click Turn on… to grant the Accessibility permission. Where the text lands explains what it does and what it doesn't. Windows needs no permission to paste, so the line always says it is on. When the text cannot be pasted (an administrator window, a password field), it stays on the clipboard: see Where the text lands. Mode Hold to Talk (the default): records while you hold the keys and transcribes when you let go. Toggle: press once to start and again to stop. Pick Toggle for long dictations, when holding keys gets tiring. Stop after silence, under Advanced, only exists in this mode. Dictate covers both modes in use.

The shortcut recorder Click the shortcut key, or move to it with Tab and press Space or Enter. It says Press shortcut…. Press the new combination, all keys at once. It is saved as soon as it is complete. To back out, press Esc or Delete (Backspace on Windows) before you finish. Leaving the field does the same. The previous shortcut stays. A shortcut is a modifier plus one key. The key can be a letter, a digit, F1 to F24, an arrow, Space, Enter, Tab or one of . , / \ - = [ ] ' ; and the backquote. The shortcut must include ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥. ⇧ alone does not count. Without one, the recorder says Add ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ to the chord. The shortcut must include Ctrl or Alt. Shift alone does not count. Without one, the recorder says Add Ctrl or Alt to the chord. The Windows key is refused: The Windows key can't be part of the shortcut. Use Ctrl, Alt or Shift. A function key on its own (say F5) is not a valid shortcut either: add a modifier to it. When the shortcut is taken The system keeps some combinations for itself. If you record one of them, Open Whisper warns you and listens on a fallback shortcut instead. The warning reads … is reserved by macOS., with your shortcut at the start. The fallback is ⇧⌘D. Reserved: ⌘Space, ⌃Space, ⌃⌥Space, ⌘Tab, ⇧⌘3, ⇧⌘4, ⇧⌘5, ⌘Q, ⌘W. The warning reads … is reserved by Windows., with your shortcut at the start. The fallback is Ctrl+Shift+D. Reserved: Ctrl+Alt+Del, Ctrl+Shift+Esc, Ctrl+Esc, Ctrl+Space, Alt+Tab, Alt+Shift+Tab, Alt+F4, Alt+Space, Alt+Esc. If another app already uses the combination, the warning reads … could not be registered. Under either warning, Keep closes the warning and Change arms the recorder again. Record a different shortcut. Until you do, Start Recording in the Open Whisper menu still starts a dictation, and that menu item shows the shortcut actually in use. The default Ctrl+Shift+Space is also a shortcut in Word (a non-breaking space) and in VS Code. If you use them, record another one. In Hold to Talk, Esc cannot cancel a recording held with Ctrl+Shift+Space, because Ctrl+Shift+Esc belongs to Task Manager. A shortcut such as Ctrl+Alt+Space cancels with Ctrl+Alt+Esc. Dictate has the details.

Transcription Language Auto-detect (the default) lets the model recognise the language in each dictation, so you can switch languages from one dictation to the next. You can also pin one of 16 languages: Portuguese, English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Dutch, Russian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hindi, Polish, Turkish, Ukrainian. Pin a language if you always speak the same one: the transcription is more accurate than with auto-detect. The change applies to the next dictation. The video window uses this setting too.

Advanced Click Advanced to open the section. It holds four options: Model, Max recording, Stop after silence and Open at login, which has its own section below. Model The speech model that transcribes your dictations. The list shows each one by name and size: Default (bundled), Light, Large and Most accurate. Below it: Non-bundled models are downloaded once. Choosing a model that is not on the computer starts its download, with a progress bar. When it is done, the next dictation uses it, without a restart. If the download fails, the window says Download failed. The current model is still in use. and the choice goes back. Models explains each model and when to change. Max recording How long one dictation can last, in seconds: from 15 to 1800 (30 minutes). The default is 120. Type a number, or use the arrow buttons (one second per click, ten with Shift held). A number outside the range is brought back inside it. When a recording reaches the limit, it stops, and what was captured is transcribed and pasted. The notification says Recording stopped at the time limit — transcribing what was captured. Raise the limit if this cuts your long dictations. Stop after silence Shown only in Toggle mode. Off by default. Press On to turn it on: the readout starts at 2 seconds, and later remembers the last value you used. Change it with the arrow keys or the buttons, in steps of half a second, from 1 to 10 seconds. Going below 1 second turns it off. Once you've spoken, this much silence ends the recording. Silence before your first word never ends it, and neither do pauses shorter than the setting. The text is pasted as usual. If you press the shortcut within 1.5 seconds after it stopped by itself, the press counts as your "stop" and does not start a new recording. A last phrase spoken very quietly may be left out when the recording ends by itself. Speak at your normal volume to the end, or stop with the shortcut.

Open at login Open at login starts Open Whisper when you sign in to the computer, so the shortcut works without opening the app first. It is off by default. Press On to turn it on or off. The switch belongs to the system, not to the app: it always shows what the system says. If you turn it off in the system settings, the window shows it off the next time it comes to the front. Hint: Open Whisper is in the menu bar from the moment you log in. macOS may show its own notice that a login item was added. You can also turn it off in System Settings → General → Login Items. The switch only works for a copy placed directly in /Applications or ~/Applications. Not in a subfolder, not run from the .dmg, not opened from Downloads. Click Open System Settings and check the entry.     macOS did not accept the change. Try again or check System Settings.   Press the switch again.     Could not read the state from macOS. Install it with the installer and open that copy.     Turned off in Windows Settings → Apps → Startup. Switch it on there, or here again. Every field of the Settings window: the shortcut, the mode, the language and the four advanced options.

What a model is A speech model is a large file that has learned to recognise speech. Open Whisper runs it on your computer: the audio goes into the model, the text comes out, and nothing is sent anywhere. The models are versions of Whisper, prepared to run on a normal computer. A bigger model usually makes fewer mistakes, and takes more disk space and more time. All four models are multilingual: each one understands every language in Language, and auto-detect. Dictation and video each have their own model choice, so you can keep a fast one for dictation and a careful one for video. Next to the model, the app ships a small voice detector that tells speech from noise. It is not something you choose.

The four models   Name in the app   Id   Size   Where it comes from    --- --- --- ---    Default   small-q5_1   about 181 MB   bundled with the app     Light   base   141 MB   download     Large   medium-q5_0   514 MB   download     Most accurate   large-v3-turbo-q5_0   547 MB   download   Default is the model the app starts with, for dictation and for video. It is already on the computer and always available. Light is smaller and faster than Default, and makes more mistakes. Large and Most accurate make fewer mistakes, and are slower. They are meant for video, where you are not waiting at the cursor. The ids are the names the command line uses in --model.

Choosing a model For dictation Open Settings… from the Open Whisper menu. Click Advanced. In Model, choose one. If it is not on the computer yet, the download starts. The next dictation uses the new model, without a restart. If a model fails to load, the app keeps using the one it had. Keep Default unless you have a reason to change. A dictation should be pasted within a few seconds, and the two bigger models can make you wait. Try Light if your dictations feel slow. On Windows the transcription runs on the processor, with no graphics card acceleration. The size of the model weighs on the waiting time. For video In the video window, open Quality and choose a Model there. This choice is separate from the dictation one. Next to each model the window says whether it is already bundled, a one-time … download or …, already downloaded, and, for the two smaller ones, the error rate measured in Portuguese. The window puts it this way: Bigger models get less wrong — especially English words spoken inside Portuguese. In exchange they take disk space and time. See Video and files.

Downloading a model Choosing a model that is not on the computer, in Settings or in the video window, downloads it. A model is downloaded once; after that it stays on the computer, for dictation, video and the command line alike. The file comes from Hugging Face, from https://huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp. This is one of the few times Open Whisper uses the network, and it only happens when you choose a model. Never during a dictation. Privacy has the full list. When the download ends, the app checks the file against its known SHA-256 fingerprint. A damaged or incomplete file is not used. A download cannot start while a dictation is in progress. Wait for it to end. Settings says Download failed. The current model is still in use. The video window says Could not download the model. The previous one is still in use. Nothing changed. Check the internet connection and choose the model again.

Where the models are Downloaded models: ~/Library/Application Support/open-whisper/models/ (base.bin, medium-q5_0.bin, large-v3-turbo-q5_0.bin). The bundled model is inside the app: Open Whisper.app/Contents/Resources/models/. Downloaded models: %LOCALAPPDATA%\open-whisper\models\ (base.bin, medium-q5_0.bin, large-v3-turbo-q5_0.bin). This folder is kept out of a roaming profile. The bundled model is in the models folder where Open Whisper was installed.

What is not possible There is no button to remove a downloaded model. To free the space, first choose another model in Settings and in the video window, then delete the file from the folder above. Only these four models. You cannot add another model file, or use an online engine. The command line never downloads a model. It uses only the ones already on the computer, and stops with exit status 4 when the model is missing. The notification Couldn't load the speech model. Check Settings. means the chosen model file is missing or damaged. In Settings → Advanced → Model, choose Default: it is inside the app and always there. More in Troubleshooting.
The four speech models, what each one is for, how a download works and where the files live.

The video window Open the Open Whisper menu, in the menu bar (Mac) or the notification area (Windows). Choose Transcribe YouTube Video…. The same window takes local files too. The window is headed Transcribe video. It has a Video link field, a Choose a file… button, and a Quality section, closed until you open it. You can resize the window; only the transcript box scrolls. The window shows one notice at the top: This feature contacts YouTube to fetch the video's captions or audio. Dictation stays 100% local: no microphone audio ever leaves your Mac. This feature contacts YouTube to fetch the video's captions or audio. Dictation stays 100% local: no microphone audio ever leaves your PC. A link uses the network; a file on your computer does not. Privacy lists every use of the network.

From a YouTube link Open Whisper reaches YouTube through yt-dlp, a free tool from another project. You install it once. The app never installs or updates it for you, and a local file never needs it. Install it with Homebrew: Update it with brew upgrade yt-dlp. Install it with winget, in Command Prompt or PowerShell: Update it with winget upgrade yt-dlp.yt-dlp. A copy installed with Scoop or Chocolatey is found too. Open Whisper needs yt-dlp 2025.01.01 or newer. It checks when the window opens and each time you press Transcribe. If yt-dlp is missing or too old, the window says so, with the command to run. YouTube changes often; when links that used to work start failing, update yt-dlp first. Copy the video's link. If the clipboard holds a video link when the window opens, the field is already filled. Paste it into Video link. Press Enter or click Transcribe. The link must point to one video: youtube.com/watch?v=…, youtu.be/…, or a Shorts, embed or /live/ link. Playlists, channels, @ pages, searches and other sites are refused before anything runs.

section: From a file on your computer
text: From a file on your computer Click Choose a file…. The panel opens in your Movies folder (Mac) or Videos folder (Windows). Pick the file. The transcription starts right away. Or drag the file from the Finder or the Explorer and drop it on the window. One file at a time: if you drop several, the window says One file at a time — … were dropped. The file is read where it is. Nothing is copied, nothing is written next to it, and nothing leaves the computer. Only its sound is used: the main audio track, up to 3 hours long.   Container   Audio it can read    --- ---    MP4, M4A, MOV, 3GP   AAC, ALAC, PCM, MP3     MKV, WebM   Vorbis, FLAC, AAC, MP3, PCM     OGG   Vorbis, FLAC     MP3, FLAC, WAV, AIFF, CAF   the file's own audio   Refused, with the name of what is missing: Opus audio (in WebM, MKV or OGG), AC-3, E-AC-3 and DTS audio, and the AVI, WMV and ASF containers. Export the file again as MP4 or M4A with AAC, or as MP3, FLAC or WAV, and it works.

Captions or this device A video link can be transcribed in two ways. Open Whisper asks, for each video, and never decides for you. When the video has captions: This video has captions. Using them is almost instant. Choose Use the captions, or Transcribe on this device anyway to have Open Whisper listen to the audio itself. When it has none: This video has no usable captions. Open Whisper can transcribe the audio here on your Mac — that downloads the audio and takes a few minutes. Choose Transcribe on this device, or Cancel. This video has no usable captions. Open Whisper can transcribe the audio here on your PC — that downloads the audio and takes a few minutes. Choose Transcribe on this device, or Cancel. Captions written by a person are preferred to automatic ones. If you pinned a Language in Settings, captions in that language come first; otherwise, the video's original language. On this device, the audio is downloaded into memory, transcribed, and thrown away; it is never saved. A file is always transcribed on this device: there is nothing to choose.

Quality Open Quality to see two choices. Closed, it shows them in one line: Speed: … · Model: …. Speed has three settings. Accurate is the default.   Speed   What the window says    --- ---    Fast   The fastest. On hard passages it makes more mistakes, and a passage that comes out badly is redone.     Balanced   Makes fewer mistakes than Fast and, since it redoes fewer passages, often finishes before it.     Accurate   The most careful: the best the chosen model can do, and the slowest.   Model offers the same four models as dictation, chosen separately. The default is the bundled one. Choosing one that is not on the computer downloads it first: Downloading the model… this can take a while. See Models. Both choices are remembered, and are the starting point for the command line too. They never change dictation. The language comes from Language in Settings: pin it if you know the language of the video.

Progress and cancelling The Progress section shows a percentage, a bar and the current step: Looking up the video…, Fetching the captions…, Downloading the audio…, Preparing the audio…, Transcribing on this device…. Cancel stops the job within about two seconds. Whatever was already transcribed stays, marked as partial. If you dictate while a video runs, the video waits: Paused while you dictate — it will carry on by itself. Repetition detected — transcribing again from the start… means the model got stuck repeating itself, and Open Whisper started over. You need do nothing. Open Whisper transcribes one video at a time. Wait for the current one, or cancel it, before starting another. While a video runs, the menu shows its percentage next to Transcribe YouTube Video…. Quitting asks first: A video transcription is still running. Quitting now will lose it. Choose Keep running or Quit anyway.

The transcript One line says where the text came from: Captions written by a person, Captions generated automatically by YouTube or Transcribed on this device by Open Whisper. A notice may follow: Partial transcript — the job stopped early, but nothing already produced was lost. Excessively repeated passages were trimmed. This usually happens over music or long silence. No speech found in this video. When it transcribes on the device, Open Whisper leaves out lines it heard over silence or noise with no voice, and subtitle credit lines the model sometimes invents. Captions are kept exactly as they are. Format Text: a short header (title, channel, date, duration, link or file, language, source), then the text in paragraphs. Subtitles (SRT): timed lines, for video players and editors. Subtitles (VTT): timed lines for the web, with the header as a note. Copy and save Copy puts the transcript, in the chosen format, on the clipboard: Copied. Save writes the file right away, without asking, named after the video's title. It never overwrites: a second save becomes Title (2).txt. The window says Saved to …, followed by the path. Save As… asks where, starting in your Downloads folder. Cancelling writes nothing. Save writes to ~/.open-whisper/transcripts/. The folder is hidden in the Finder: click Show in Finder after saving, or press ⇧⌘G in the Finder and type ~/.open-whisper/transcripts. Save writes to %USERPROFILE%\.open-whisper\transcripts\. Click Show in Explorer after saving to open it. Closing the window If you close the window before copying or saving, it asks: Close without copying or saving? The transcript is still here when you reopen this window. Choose Go back or Close anyway. The transcript waits in the window until you start another one, or quit the app.

Turn a YouTube video or an audio or video file into text or subtitles, from the video window.

What it is for Turning a recording into text or subtitles without opening a window. Feeding a transcript to another program, in JSON with the time of each sentence and, if you ask, of each word. Running the same transcription again with the same options. The command is part of the app: there is nothing else to install. It reads your settings (the video window's Speed and Model, and the Language) as its defaults, and never changes them. It never writes a file, and dictation keeps working while it runs.

Getting the command If you installed with Homebrew, open-whisper is already on the PATH. If you installed from the .dmg, link it once. On a Mac with Apple Silicon: On an Intel Mac, link it into /usr/local/bin/open-whisper instead. Check it in Terminal: It prints open-whisper followed by the version. With no arguments, open-whisper starts the menu-bar app instead. The installer adds Open Whisper's folder to your user PATH. Open a new Command Prompt or PowerShell window after installing (one that was already open does not see the change), then check it: It prints open-whisper followed by the version. open-whisper runs open-whisper.com, the console version of the app, so the terminal waits for it and shows its output. With no arguments it stops with a usage error: the app itself starts from the Start menu. If your PATH was already very long, the installer leaves it alone. Run the command by its full path then: open-whisper.com in the folder where Open Whisper was installed, usually %LOCALAPPDATA%\Open Whisper. Put a path with spaces in quotes. A relative path is read from the folder the terminal is in.

Recipes 1. A file to text The text is the same as the video window's Copy with Text: a short header, then the transcript. Any file the video window accepts works here too; see Video and files. 2. Subtitles The files are the same ones the window's Save writes. 3. JSON for another program The full text is in transcript.text, each sentence with its start and end in transcript.segments, and the settings used in settings. New fields may appear over time; existing ones keep their names. 4. The time of each word Each segment gains a words list, with each word's start, end and a confidence from 0 to 1. Use it to cut pauses or false starts inside a sentence. It only works with --format json, and only for a transcription made on this device: captions have no word times. 5. Numbers as they were said By default the engine writes numbers as figures ("310"). With --numbers spoken it writes them in words, as spoken, and no figure appears anywhere. Useful for checking a narration against its script. A Roman numeral is made of letters and may stay as it is, and next to a number the engine sometimes slips in a short extra word. It only applies on this device, not to captions. 6. Names it gets wrong --prompt gives the engine the spellings of names and jargon, for this call only. List the words; do not write a sentence. A file's name never influences its transcript, so this is the only way to hint a file. 7. Pinning the language Pinning the language spoken in the recording is more accurate than auto-detect. --lang auto detects it. The codes are those of the 16 languages in Settings: pt, en, es, fr, de, it, nl, ru, zh, ja, ko, ar, hi, pl, tr, uk. Any other code is a usage error. 8. A YouTube link Put the link in quotes. Without --on-device, the command uses the video's captions when there are usable ones, which takes seconds. With --on-device, it downloads the audio and transcribes it on the computer; that flag is your consent, like the choice in the window. A video with no usable captions and no --on-device stops with exit status 7. Links need yt-dlp, as in the video window. 9. A different model or speed The model must already be on the computer: the command never downloads one, and stops with exit status 4 if it is missing. Download it in Settings or in the video window (Models). --model small-q5_1, the bundled model, always works.

What comes out where The result goes to standard output, and nothing else: complete, then the command ends with status 0. On any failure it stays empty, so a half transcript never reaches your file. Everything else goes to standard error: progress lines that start with open-whisper:, the one-line reason when it fails, and the engine's own messages. Its wording may change, and it is safe to discard. Read the output only when the status is 0. To see the status of the last command: In Command Prompt, echo %ERRORLEVEL%. In PowerShell, $LASTEXITCODE. Each status has its own meaning (4 is a missing model, 5 an unsupported format, 7 a video that needs --on-device…). The whole table, with what to do for each, is in Command reference.

The network A file on your computer uses no network at all. A YouTube link uses the network only to fetch the video. Before it fetches anything, the command says so on standard error: open-whisper: fetching the video from the network — the transcription itself stays on this machine.

Timing and stopping On a Mac with Apple Silicon and the bundled model, an hour of audio takes about three minutes; the first call also spends a second or two loading the model. A link with usable captions returns in seconds. To stop, press Ctrl+C. The command ends within about two seconds, with status 130, and delivers nothing. The command does one input per call: no folders, no lists, no playlists. To transcribe many files, run it once per file, in a loop of your shell.
Transcribe a file or a video from the terminal with open-whisper transcribe, in text, subtitles or JSON.

What stays on your computer Your voice. The audio is held in memory while you dictate and discarded after the transcription. It is never written to disk. The transcription. It runs on your computer, with no network at all. Dictation works the same with the internet off. The text. It goes where your cursor is, or to the clipboard. Open Whisper keeps the last dictation in memory so Copy Last Transcription and Retry Last Transcription work. It is gone when you quit. There is no history. Video files on your computer. A file you transcribe is read where it is. Nothing is copied, and no network is used.

section: The only things that use the internet
text: The only things that use the internet Nothing on this list happens during a dictation.   What   When   Where it goes    --- --- ---    Downloading an optional model   Only when you choose a model that isn't bundled, in Settings or the video window. Once per model.   huggingface.co. The file is checked before it is used.     Transcribing a YouTube video   Only when you paste a video link and ask for it.   YouTube, to fetch the captions or the audio. The window says so before anything runs.     The Made by entringer.dev link in About   Only when you click it.   Your browser opens the page. The app itself sends nothing.     The Windows installer   Only during installation, and only if Windows lacks WebView2.   Microsoft, to download WebView2.   For a video link, the audio is fetched by yt-dlp, a separate tool you install yourself. Once the audio is on your computer, the transcription itself uses no network. See Video and files.

No account, no analytics No account, no sign-up, no API key. No analytics, no telemetry, no crash reports. No update check. Open Whisper never calls home to look for a new version. New versions are announced on the Releases page. No log files. Open Whisper writes nothing about what you do.

The clipboard To paste, Open Whisper puts the text on the clipboard and presses paste for you. When the paste works, the text that was on the clipboard before is put back half a second later. Only text is put back: an image or other content you had copied may not come back. When the text can't be pasted, it stays on the clipboard so nothing is lost, and a notice says Copied to clipboard — paste with ⌘V. When the paste works, the text that was on the clipboard before is put back half a second later. Only text is put back: an image or other content you had copied may not come back. When the text can't be pasted, it stays on the clipboard so nothing is lost, and a notice says Copied to clipboard — paste with Ctrl+V. Every dictated text is kept out of the clipboard history (Win+V) and out of cloud clipboard sync. That holds when the text stays on the clipboard too: it never appears in Win+V, and it never reaches your other devices.

Transcripts you save Dictations are never saved. A video transcript is saved only when you click Save or Save As… in the video window. Save writes to ~/.open-whisper/transcripts/. That folder is hidden in Finder and is created the first time you save. Save writes to %USERPROFILE%\.open-whisper\transcripts\. That folder is created the first time you save. Save As… writes where you choose. The command line never writes a file. Every location the app uses is in Data and uninstalling.

What the permissions are for Microphone: used only while you dictate, never in the background. Accessibility: used only to send ⌘V to the app you're in. To decide whether to paste, Open Whisper asks macOS what kind of field has focus (whether you can type in it, whether it is a password field). It never reads your screen or what you type. Microphone: used only while you dictate, never in the background. There is no Accessibility permission on Windows. To decide whether to paste, Open Whisper asks Windows what kind of field has focus (whether you can type in it, whether it is a password field). It never reads your screen or what you type.

Check it yourself You don't have to take this on trust. Watch the app's network traffic while you dictate. Open a network monitor, such as Little Snitch, or run nettop in Terminal. Find Open Whisper (its process is called open-whisper). Dictate a few sentences. No connection appears. For a second test, turn Wi-Fi off and dictate again. It works the same. Open Resource Monitor: type resmon in the Start menu and press Enter. Go to the Network tab and tick Open Whisper's process in the list, so only its traffic shows. Dictate a few sentences. No connection appears. For a second test, disconnect from the internet and dictate again. It works the same. You will see traffic only when you do one of the things in the table above: downloading a model or transcribing a YouTube link.
What stays on your computer, the few things that use the internet and when, and how to check it yourself.

Installing "Windows protected your PC" The installer isn't signed yet, so SmartScreen doesn't recognise it. The warning is expected. Check the file first: in the folder where you downloaded it, run certutil -hashfile Open.Whisper_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe SHA256 (with your version's file name). Compare the result with the hash in the .sha256 file from the same release. They must match. Open the installer again and click More info, then Run anyway. The installer needs the internet If Windows lacks WebView2, the installer downloads it during installation. Connect to the internet and run the installer again. Open Whisper itself doesn't need the internet afterwards. Your processor is older On Windows, Open Whisper needs a processor with AVX2 (Intel from 2013, AMD from 2015). An older processor is not supported. The app doesn't seem to open Open Whisper has no window and no Dock or taskbar button. It lives in one icon. Look in the menu bar, near the clock. Click the icon to open the menu. Look in the notification area, next to the clock. If you don't see it, click ^ (show hidden icons) and drag the Open Whisper icon onto the taskbar. Starting the app a second time does nothing visible: the copy that is already running stays in charge. "Open at login" can't be turned on The message Move Open Whisper to the Applications folder to use this option. means the app is running from somewhere else: the .dmg, Downloads, or a subfolder. Quit Open Whisper. Move Open Whisper.app directly into /Applications (not into a subfolder such as Utilities). Open it from there and turn the option on again. If it says Approve Open Whisper in System Settings → Login Items., click Open System Settings and switch Open Whisper on under Login Items. The message Install Open Whisper with its installer to use this option. means this copy isn't the one the installer put on your PC. Install it with the installer and open that copy. If it says Turned off in Windows Settings → Apps → Startup., the option was switched off in Windows. Turn it on again in Open Whisper, or click Open Windows Settings and switch it on under Startup.

Permissions Microphone access is off Dictation needs the microphone. If you refused it, or setup says Microphone access is off: Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone. Switch Open Whisper on. Dictate again. Windows lets apps use the microphone unless it was turned off in its settings. When it is off, Open Whisper doesn't record and says so: Windows is blocking the microphone. Allow it in Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone, including for desktop apps. Open Whisper's Settings show the same line at the top of Recording, with the key Open Windows Settings. Open Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone. Turn on microphone access at the top of the page, and Let desktop apps access your microphone. Dictate again. Auto-paste won't turn on (Mac) macOS applies the Accessibility permission only when the app opens again. If the switch in System Settings is on but the text still goes to the clipboard: Quit Open Whisper from its menu (Quit Open Whisper) and open it again. During setup, Reopen Open Whisper does this for you. If the switch keeps flipping back off, make sure you're using the copy from the official download. Still stuck? Clear the permission in Terminal and grant it again: tccutil reset Accessibility dev.entringer.openwhisper Choose Enable auto-paste… in the menu, switch Open Whisper on, and reopen the app. There is no Accessibility permission on Windows: auto-paste is always available. If the text isn't pasted, see The text was not pasted.

The shortcut Pressing the shortcut does nothing Open the menu and look at Start Recording: the key shown beside it is the shortcut that is really active. If another app already uses your combination, Settings says … could not be registered. Pick another combination in Settings. Until then, Start Recording in the menu always works. If the shortcut works but nothing is pasted, see Recording and The text was not pasted. "… is reserved by macOS" or "… is reserved by Windows" The system keeps that combination for itself. While it is chosen, Open Whisper uses ⇧⌘D on the Mac or Ctrl+Shift+D on Windows instead. In Settings, click Change and press another combination. Or click Keep and use the fallback shown beside Start Recording in the menu. The full list of reserved combinations is in Shortcuts and keys. The recorder doesn't accept the combination A shortcut needs a modifier. A key on its own, even a function key such as F5, can't be the shortcut. Include ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥. Shift alone doesn't count. If you see Could not save preferences, the combination has no modifier: press it again with one. Include Ctrl or Alt. Shift alone doesn't count, and the Windows key can't be part of the shortcut. If you see Could not save preferences, the combination has no modifier: press it again with one. The shortcut gets in the way of another app On Windows, Ctrl+Shift+Space also means something in Word and VS Code. Choose another combination in Settings, such as Ctrl+Alt+Space. Esc doesn't cancel Esc cancels only while Open Whisper says Recording. Once it says Transcribing, the recording is over and Esc no longer cancels. In Hold to Talk, press Esc while you still hold the shortcut. Both work: Esc alone, or the held keys plus Esc. If your shortcut holds both ⌥ and ⌘, ⌥⌘Esc belongs to macOS (Force Quit): use Toggle mode to cancel with Esc. In Hold to Talk with Ctrl+Shift+Space, Esc can't cancel: Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager. Either: Release the keys: the recording ends and is transcribed as usual. Switch to Toggle mode, where Esc cancels. Or choose a shortcut such as Ctrl+Alt+Space, which cancels with Ctrl+Alt+Esc.

Recording "Microphone unavailable — check the permission or whether another app is using it." No microphone was found, or another app is holding it. Check that a microphone is connected and selected in the system's sound settings. Close the app that is using it (a call, a recorder) and try again. If that isn't it, check the permission (see Permissions). "Nothing was recorded — check the microphone permission, or hold the shortcut a moment longer." The press was too short to capture any audio, or the microphone gave nothing. Hold the shortcut, start speaking, and release only after the last word. If it keeps happening, check the permission (see Permissions). Nothing happens after you speak When no speech was heard, nothing is pasted and there is no notice, only the closing sound. Speak a little closer to the microphone and try again. On Windows, also check that the microphone isn't blocked (see Permissions). The recording stopped by itself Two settings can end a recording: Max recording: at the limit (120 seconds by default) the recording stops and what was captured is transcribed. A notice says Recording stopped at the time limit — transcribing what was captured. Raise it up to 1800 seconds in Settings, under Advanced. Stop after silence (Toggle mode only): after you've spoken, that much silence ends the recording. Raise the time or turn it off in Advanced. A phrase spoken very quietly at the very end can be left out. "Couldn't load the speech model. Check Settings." The model you chose is missing or damaged. Open Settings and expand Advanced. Under Model, choose Default (the bundled one). If that fails too, reinstall Open Whisper. "Download failed. The current model is still in use." The model didn't download. The previous one keeps working. Check your internet connection. Choose the model again in Advanced → Model to retry. A download can't start during a dictation. Words come out wrong, or in the wrong language In Settings, set Language to the language you speak instead of Auto-detect. Larger models make fewer mistakes, in exchange for a download and more time: see Models.

The text was not pasted A notice says "Copied to clipboard" The text couldn't be pasted where you were, so it was kept on the clipboard. Nothing was lost. It happens when auto-paste is off (Settings shows Automatic paste: off), in a password field, or when nothing you can type in has focus (the desktop, a Finder window, a page you're only reading). Click where the text should go. Press ⌘V, or choose Retry Last Transcription in the menu. To paste automatically from now on, click Turn on… in Settings, or Enable auto-paste… in the menu. It happens in a window opened as administrator (Windows doesn't let other apps type into it), in a password field, or when nothing you can type in has focus. Click where the text should go. Press Ctrl+V, or choose Retry Last Transcription in the menu. Running Open Whisper itself as administrator is not recommended. The text appeared nowhere In browsers and apps built on them (Chrome, VS Code, Slack, Discord), Open Whisper can't always tell whether a text field has focus, so it pastes anyway. If no field had focus, the paste lands nowhere and the clipboard goes back to what it held before. Click in the field. Choose Copy Last Transcription in the menu, then paste. The last dictation is kept until you quit. Dictations don't show in Windows clipboard history This is on purpose. Dictated text never goes into Win+V or cloud clipboard sync, even when it stays on the clipboard. See Privacy. What you had copied didn't come back After a paste, Open Whisper puts back what the clipboard held, but only text. An image or other content you had copied may not come back.

Video "Open Whisper needs yt-dlp to reach videos" Video links need yt-dlp, a free tool you install yourself. Open Whisper never installs or updates it. Files on your computer don't need it. If it says the installed yt-dlp is too old (2025.01.01 is the minimum): If it says the installed yt-dlp is too old (2025.01.01 is the minimum): If yt-dlp is installed somewhere Open Whisper doesn't look, set the OPEN_WHISPER_YT_DLP environment variable to its full path. "It failed for a reason Open Whisper does not recognize" YouTube changes often, and an older yt-dlp stops working. Update yt-dlp (above) and try again. "That is not a YouTube video link" Only links to a single YouTube video work. Playlists, channels and other sites are refused. Open the video itself and copy its link. "This video has no usable captions" Click Transcribe on this device. It downloads the audio and transcribes it on your computer, which takes a few minutes. "YouTube is rate-limiting requests right now" or "No internet connection." Wait a few minutes, check your connection, and try again. "Open Whisper cannot decode this file's audio" The file uses a format the app can't read (Opus, AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS, or an AVI, WMV or ASF file). Export it as MP4 or M4A with AAC, or as MP3, FLAC or WAV, and try again. "This video is longer than the 3-hour limit" Videos and files over 3 hours don't fit safely in memory. Cut the recording into parts under 3 hours. "Open Whisper transcribes one video at a time" Wait for the current job or cancel it. Copy is also refused while you dictate: wait for the dictation to finish and click it again. The video comes out in the language you used before If you changed Language in Settings and a video still comes out in the old one, quit Open Whisper and open it again. Quitting asks about a video A video transcription is still running. Quitting now will lose it. Click Keep running to let it finish, or Quit anyway to lose it.

Command line "open-whisper" is not found If you installed with Homebrew, the command is already on your PATH. If you installed from the .dmg, link it once: On an Intel Mac, use /usr/local/bin/open-whisper as the last part. Open a new terminal window: windows that were open during the installation don't see the command yet. If it still isn't found, your PATH was too long for the installer to add it. Run open-whisper.com by its full path, in the folder where Open Whisper is installed. Running open-whisper with no arguments stops with a usage error on purpose: the app itself starts from the Start menu. Exit status 2 The command was mistyped: an unknown option or value, a missing input, two inputs, or an input given without transcribe. Run open-whisper --help and check the command. Exit status 4 The model isn't downloaded, and the command never downloads anything. Add --model small-q5_1 to use the bundled one, or download the model in the app first. Exit status 7 The video has no usable captions. Run it again with --on-device to transcribe the audio on your computer. Every exit status, with what to do, is in the Command reference.
Still stuck? If your problem isn't here, or a fix didn't work, tell us. Reporting a problem explains where and what to include.
Every known problem, by what you see: the cause and the steps that fix it, on Mac and Windows.

Price and account Is it really free? Yes. Open Whisper is free to install and use, for personal or professional work, on as many computers as you like. There is no subscription and no trial. The terms of use say so in writing. Does it need an account? No. There is no account, no sign-up and no API key. You install it and use it.

Privacy and the internet Does my voice leave the computer? No. The audio stays in memory while you dictate, is transcribed on your computer and is then discarded. It is never written to disk and never sent anywhere. You can check it with a network monitor: see Privacy. Does it work offline? Yes. Dictation never uses the internet. Only two optional things do: downloading a larger model, and transcribing a YouTube link. Transcribing a video file from your computer works offline too. See Privacy.

Windows and Mac Why does Windows warn about the installer? The first Windows installer isn't signed yet, so Windows shows Windows protected your PC. Check the file's hash, then click More info and Run anyway. The steps are in Install. When is the Mac version coming? The Mac version ships once Apple has signed and notarized it. It will install with Homebrew or a .dmg. There is no date: follow the Releases page to hear when it's out.

Using it Which languages does it understand? By default it detects the language you speak, each time you dictate, so you can switch languages between dictations. You can also pin one of 16 languages in Settings for better results. The app's own screens are in English or Portuguese, following your system's language. Can I change the shortcut? Yes, during setup or in Settings. The default is ⇧⌘Space on the Mac and Ctrl+Shift+Space on Windows. A shortcut needs a modifier, such as ⌘ or Ctrl. All keys are in Shortcuts and keys. Does it work in any app? It pastes wherever a normal paste works: browsers, editors, chat apps, documents. When it can't paste (a password field, or a window opened as administrator on Windows), the text stays on the clipboard and you paste it yourself. Nothing is lost. See Where the text lands. What doesn't it do? It writes down what you say, where your cursor is. It doesn't rewrite your text with AI, record meetings, translate, or keep a history. The full list, with the reason for each, is in What Open Whisper doesn't do.
Short answers to what people ask first: price, the internet, languages, Windows and Mac, the shortcut.

Change it during setup or in Settings. The key shown beside Start Recording in the menu is always the one really active.

Cancelling a recording Esc is taken only while Open Whisper is recording. The rest of the time it reaches your apps untouched. Once the recording becomes Transcribing, Esc no longer cancels. These belong to the system. If you choose one, Settings says it is reserved and the fallback above is used.
