Synopsis <INPUT> is one media file or one video link per call. A path that exists is a file; anything else must be a link to a single YouTube video. Put quotes around a path with spaces. Options may come before or after the input, as --option value or --option=value. -- ends the options. --version prints open-whisper and the version, such as open-whisper 0.1.0. The command reads the preferences you set in the app and never changes them. With no arguments, open-whisper starts the menu-bar app instead. With no arguments, open-whisper stops with a usage error (status 2): the app itself starts from the Start menu. The command works in Command Prompt and PowerShell.

Options   Option   Values   Default   What it does    --- --- --- ---    --format   txt, srt, vtt, json   txt   The output format (see below).     --on-device   none   off   For a link: skip the captions and transcribe the audio on this computer. This flag is your consent, never assumed. A file is always transcribed on this computer.     --words   none   off   With --format json only: each segment gets a list of words with their times. Captions carry no word times.     --prompt   text   none   A vocabulary hint (names, jargon) for this call. For a link it replaces the hint taken from the title and channel. An empty value means no hint.     --numbers   written, spoken   written   spoken writes numbers in words, as said, with no figures. Roman numerals are letters and may stay. Applies only to what is transcribed on this computer, not to captions.     --model   small-q5_1, base, medium-q5_0, large-v3-turbo-q5_0   the video model set in the app   The model for this call. It must already be downloaded: the command never downloads (status 4).     --quality   fast, balanced, accurate   the video speed set in the app   The speed for this call.     --lang   pt, en, es, fr, de, it, nl, ru, zh, ja, ko, ar, hi, pl, tr, uk, or auto   the Language set in the app   The language for this call. An unknown code is status 2. Pinning the language usually gives better results than auto.   small-q5_1 is the bundled model. The others are downloaded once in the app: see Models.

Output formats   Format   What you get    --- ---    txt   Plain text, with a header (title, channel, publication date, duration, link or file, language, source) and a paragraph break wherever speech pauses for more than 2 seconds.     srt   Subtitles (SRT), with no header.     vtt   Subtitles (WebVTT), with the header as a NOTE block.     json   One JSON document with the transcript, its segments and how it was made (see below).   txt, srt and vtt are identical, byte for byte, to what Copy and Save give in the video window.

The two streams Standard output carries only the result, in UTF-8 with \n line endings. It is written in full, then the command exits with status 0. On any failure it is empty, so a script never mistakes a message for a transcript. Standard error carries everything else, for people: a line before any network use (links only), progress, and one line explaining a failure. These lines may change; don't parse them. Standard input is ignored. Some standard error lines you may see:

The JSON envelope With --format json, standard output holds one JSON document. Fields are added over time but never removed or renamed, so ignore fields you don't know.   Field   What it holds    --- ---    app   name and version.     input   kind (file or url), reference (the path or link), title, duration_secs, and for a file audio (sample rate, channels, track, container, codec).     settings.model   The model id, and origin: preferences or override (you passed --model).     settings.quality   value and origin.     settings.language   requested, origin, and detected (the language heard).     settings.prompt   value and origin: override, video_metadata or none.     settings.numbers   value, and applied: true when transcribed on this computer, false for captions.     transcript.provenance   on_device, manual_captions or automatic_captions.     transcript.language   The transcript's language.     transcript.repetition_flagged   true when excessively repeated passages were trimmed.     transcript.segments   Each with start_ms, end_ms, text; words with --words; suspect: true on a line that looks like a channel sign-off.     transcript.text   The whole text.     transcript.empty_reason   no_speech, only when no segment is left. The status is still 0.     transcript.suppressed   Segments set aside as not speech, each with start_ms, end_ms, text and reason (silence, subtitle_credit or no_speech). Present only when there are some.     transcript.word_timestamps   With --words: whether word times are available. For captions, available: false with reason: captions.   Each item in words has start_ms, end_ms, text and probability. The words, in order, are the segment's text split on spaces. Each lasts at least 40 ms, words never overlap and they stay inside their segment. probability goes from 0 to 1 and is relative, not a calibrated score.

Exit statuses   Status   Meaning   What to do    --- --- ---    0   The transcript is on standard output. Also when no speech was found (see empty_reason).   Read standard output.     1   Internal error.   Report it with the standard error line.     2   Usage error: unknown option or value, missing or extra input, unknown --lang or --model, an input without transcribe, a link that isn't a single YouTube video.   Fix the command. open-whisper --help shows the usage.     3   yt-dlp is missing or too old (links only).   Install or update yt-dlp: see Troubleshooting.     4   The model isn't downloaded.   Use --model small-q5_1, or download the model in the app.     5   Unsupported format. The message names the codec or container.   Export as MP4 or M4A with AAC, or as MP3, FLAC or WAV.     6   The file can't be read: no file there, a folder, no permission, empty or truncated, no audio track, or longer than 3 hours.   Fix the input.     7   The link has no usable captions and you didn't pass --on-device.   Run again with --on-device.     8   Video error: unavailable, private or removed, age-restricted, not available in your region, a live stream, rate-limited, no network, a decoding or transcription failure, an unrecognised failure, or another video already running.   Rate limits and network errors are worth retrying later.     9   The transcript was ready, but standard output closed before receiving it.   Run again.     130   Interrupted (Ctrl+C). The command stops within 2 seconds and delivers nothing.   Nothing to do.   Read the status in Terminal with echo $?. Read the status with echo %ERRORLEVEL% in Command Prompt, or $LASTEXITCODE in PowerShell.

Guarantees The command never writes a file, whatever happens. Redirect standard output to save the result. The input file is read where it is. Its size and modification date don't change. A file from your computer makes no network request at all. A link uses the network only to fetch the video. It never changes your preferences, and dictation keeps working while it runs. One input per call. There are no folders, wildcards or playlists: loop over files in your own script. It doesn't read subtitle tracks inside a file, choose an audio track, stream partial output, translate or summarise. On a Mac with Apple Silicon, the bundled model transcribes roughly 20 to 25 times faster than real time, so an hour of audio takes about 3 minutes, plus a second or two to load the model. On Windows the speed depends on the processor. In a script, allow at least a tenth of the recording's length plus 60 seconds before timing out.
The complete open-whisper transcribe command: every option, the formats, the two streams, the JSON fields and every exit status.

Where your data lives   What   Mac   Windows    --- --- ---    Preferences   ~/Library/Application Support/open-whisper/preferences.json   %APPDATA%\open-whisper\preferences.json     Downloaded models   ~/Library/Application Support/open-whisper/models/   %LOCALAPPDATA%\open-whisper\models\     Bundled model   inside Open Whisper.app   in the app's install folder     Saved video transcripts   ~/.open-whisper/transcripts/   %USERPROFILE%\.open-whisper\transcripts\     Open at login   System Settings → General → Login Items   Settings → Apps → Startup   What is never on disk: Audio. It stays in memory and is discarded after the transcription. Dictated text. The last dictation is kept in memory until you quit. There is no history. Logs. Open Whisper writes no log file. Anything from the command line. The command writes nothing anywhere. On Windows, downloaded models are kept in the local folder so they don't travel with a roaming profile. The transcripts folder starts with a dot, so Finder hides it. To open it, press ⇧⌘G in Finder and type ~/.open-whisper/transcripts. To open a folder, paste its path, such as %APPDATA%\open-whisper, into the File Explorer address bar.

Resetting your preferences Quit Open Whisper from its menu (Quit Open Whisper). Delete preferences.json from the folder above. Open Open Whisper again. Every setting is back to its default, and setup opens again.

Removing a downloaded model There is no button for this: delete the model's file. In Settings → Advanced → Model, choose Default, so the model you delete isn't the one in use. If it is the video model, choose Default in the video window's Quality too. Quit Open Whisper. Delete the file from the models folder above: base.bin, medium-q5_0.bin or large-v3-turbo-q5_0.bin. The bundled model can't be removed: it is part of the app.

Uninstalling With Homebrew: To remove your preferences, models and the app's other files too: The --zap option moves these to the Trash: ~/Library/Application Support/open-whisper, and the folders named dev.entringer.openwhisper in ~/Library/Caches, ~/Library/HTTPStorages, ~/Library/Saved Application State and ~/Library/WebKit, plus ~/Library/Preferences/dev.entringer.openwhisper.plist. By hand: Quit Open Whisper from its menu (Quit Open Whisper). Drag Open Whisper.app from Applications to the Trash. To remove your preferences and models, delete ~/Library/Application Support/open-whisper. The other folders listed above can go too. If you linked the command by hand, remove the link, such as /opt/homebrew/bin/open-whisper. Neither way deletes saved video transcripts in ~/.open-whisper/transcripts. Delete that folder yourself if you want them gone. Open Settings → Apps. Find Open Whisper and click Uninstall. To remove your data too, tick the box that deletes the application data.     Removed    --- ---    Always   The app, its Start menu shortcut, the open-whisper command and its PATH entry, and Open at login.     Only if you tick the box   Your preferences (%APPDATA%\open-whisper) and downloaded models (%LOCALAPPDATA%\open-whisper).     Never   Saved video transcripts in %USERPROFILE%\.open-whisper\transcripts. Delete that folder yourself if you want them gone.   Installing a new version over the old one never deletes your data.

Resetting permissions To clear the Accessibility permission, so macOS asks again from scratch, run this in Terminal: Then grant it again with Enable auto-paste… in the menu, and reopen the app. To stop Open Whisper using the microphone, switch it off in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone. Windows has no Accessibility permission. The microphone is controlled in Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone, with Let desktop apps access your microphone.
Where Open Whisper keeps preferences, models and saved transcripts, how to reset them, and how to uninstall on each platform.

Transcription stays on your computer No cloud transcription services. Sending your voice to an online service would break the promise the app is built on: your audio never leaves the device. No AI cleanup, rewriting, chat or read-aloud. Open Whisper writes down what you said. Deciding what you *meant* is a different product. No translation or summaries. Same reason: the text is what you said, in the language you said it.

Other people's voices No meeting recording. Recording other people raises consent questions that a dictation tool shouldn't answer for you. No speaker identification. Telling who said what belongs to meeting transcription, which is out for the same reason.

Files and videos Transcribing one video link or one file is a secondary feature, kept small on purpose. One at a time. No folders, playlists, channels or watched folders. The app is about the moment you're typing, not about processing a library. From the command line, you can loop over files in your own script. YouTube only. Links from other sites are refused before anything runs. No copy of the media. A file is read where it is and never copied. A video's audio is held in memory and discarded. No pasting a video transcript at your cursor. It shows in its own window, for you to copy or save. Some formats aren't read. Opus, AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS, AVI, WMV and ASF would need a second outside tool. The app names the format it can't read and tells you how to convert it. No subtitle tracks from inside a file, no choice of audio track, no live output while it works. No dictation from the command line. Dictation is the shortcut.

Your data No history. The last dictation is kept in memory until you quit, so you can copy or paste it again. Nothing else is stored. No account and no cloud sync. There is nothing to sync, because nothing leaves your computer.

Platforms and stores No Mac App Store or Microsoft Store. To paste into other apps, Open Whisper sends the paste keystroke for you. The stores' sandboxes don't allow that, so a store version couldn't do the one thing the app exists to do. On Windows, a download only. The installer comes from the Releases page, with no package-manager listing for now. No Linux or phone version yet. They are on the roadmap. No date is promised. On Windows, no native ARM build and no graphics-card acceleration yet. Windows on ARM runs the app emulated, and transcription runs on the processor.

A simple interface One icon (in the menu bar on the Mac, in the notification area on Windows) and a small Settings window. There is no main window, and the only thing you need to set up is the shortcut.

text: An edge case is weighed, not refused on sight If your idea sits close to one of these lines, suggest it anyway. An idea that needs a decision is marked for review and answered with a reason, not closed on sight. See Reporting a problem.
The things Open Whisper leaves out on purpose, and the concrete reason behind each one.

Where to report First look at Troubleshooting: the fix may already be there. Check what has already been reported. If your problem is there, add what you see to it. Otherwise, open a new issue. You need a GitHub account. Write in the language you prefer. The answer comes in the language the issue was written in.

What makes a good report What you expected, and what happened instead. "The text went to the clipboard instead of into the document" can be solved. "It doesn't work" can't. The app you were dictating into. Pasting behaves differently in a browser, a code editor and a chat app, and this is usually the deciding detail. The steps, in order, from the shortcut press to what you saw. Whether it happens every time, or only sometimes. Your system and its version: macOS 14, 15…, or Windows 10 or 11. The app version and build. Open About Open Whisper from the menu and copy the line Version … (build …): you can select it. Your mode and shortcut, if the problem is about recording: Hold to Talk or Toggle. For the command line: the command you ran, the exit status, and the last line it printed. Open Whisper writes no log file. Describe what you saw, and the notice's exact words if there was one.

Keep private text out Issues are public: anyone can read them. Don't paste what you dictated if it's private, and check that screenshots don't show it either. The content of a transcription is never needed to fix a problem with the transcription. If the problem is about the words themselves (a name always misspelled, a language mixed up), make up a sentence that shows it, and dictate that.

What to expect Every issue is read and answered. A refusal always comes with a concrete reason. "Out of scope" on its own is not an answer. No date is ever promised. "Accepted and queued" is as far as it goes. When something you reported ships, you're told on your issue. If a fix doesn't hold, reopen the issue.

The About window Open the menu: the icon in the menu bar on the Mac, in the notification area on Windows. Choose About Open Whisper. Close it with Esc. It shows: The app's name and the line Version … (build …). On-device voice transcription at your cursor. 100% local. No audio ever leaves your Mac. On Windows: 100% local. No audio ever leaves your PC. A note that Open Whisper is not affiliated with, nor endorsed by, OpenAI, and is built on the Whisper model. The link Made by entringer.dev, which opens that page in your browser.

Version and build The version, such as 0.1.0, names the release. The build number tells apart copies made for the same version. You can select the line and copy it. Paste it into any problem report. From the command line, open-whisper --version prints the version too.
